newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania, World Bank clinch $80 mln loan deal.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania, World Bank clinch $80 mln loan deal.

text.p: Lithuania said on Wednesday it had renegotiated the terms of a loan agreement with the World Bank, paving the way for the $80 million borrowing.
"We have changed some of the terms of the memorandum we signed in July," Lithuanian Finance Minister Algimantas Krizinauskas told Reuters after returning from the United States.

Krizinauskas said the World Bank had agreed to change a key condition requiring Lithuania's state enterprises and other public institutions to reduce their debt to the energy sector from 140 million litas to 22 million litas by September 19.
He gave no details concerning the new requirements.
The loan will come in two equal tranches, the first in September or October this year and the second in March 1997.
It will be used to restructure Lithuania's troubled banking, energy, agricultural and social protection sectors.
Lithuania is currently shaking off the effects of a banking crisis which broke late last year with the surprise closure of two of its top banks.
To qualify for the loan, the Lithuanian government two weeks ago refused to bail out Vakaru Bank, once the eighth largest in the Baltic state.
In the energy sector, funds from the loan will be used to cut state and local council debts to energy suppliers.
Lithuania's inefficient energy sector has been caught in a vicious circle of debt, with consumers unable to pay producers at even subsidised prices and producers unable to pay their suppliers.
In agriculture, the funds will be used to help bring Lithuania's farms up to European Union standards.

A third of Lithuania's population resides in the countryside, where farmers till tiny lots with horse-drawn ploughs. EU experts say most of the country's farms are not viable in a market economy and consolidation is inevitable.
